key_insight: Differentiable inverse rendering estimates per-pixel optical attenuation from a single OCT image by inverting a physics-based image formation model.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support quantitative characterization of vascular tissue, but clinical diagnostic benefit remains unestablished.
method: Simulate OCT image formation with a differentiable physics-based forward model.
Optimize per-pixel attenuation using gradient descent, without training data or segmentations.
Retain the optimization procedure when changing the forward model or target optical parameter.
evidence_signal: The method was verified against analytical solutions, validated on five in vitro phantoms, and applied without modification to 29,269 clinical intravascular OCT images from 128 patients.
watch_item: Clinical application does not establish tissue-level accuracy or diagnostic utility; estimates may depend on how faithfully the forward model represents acquisition physics.
paper_title: Differentiable Inverse Rendering Recovers Intrinsic Properties from Intravascular Optical Coherence Tomography
